'''Marc van Roosmalen''' (born 23 June 1947) is a Dutch-Brazilian primatologist. He was elected as one of the "Heroes for the Planet" by [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/reports/environment/heroes/heroesgallery/0,2967,roosmalen,00.html |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |title= Marc van Roosmalen |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091202085350/http://www.time.com/time/reports/environment/heroes/heroesgallery/0%2C2967%2Croosmalen%2C00.html |archivedate=December 2, 2009 }}</ref> His research has led to the identification of several new monkey species, as well as other mammals and plants, although some of these identifications are challenged.<ref name="TrialofaP">{{cite journal|last=Edinger |first=Claudio |date=February 2008 |title=Trials of a Primatologist |journal=Smithsonian |volume=38 |issue=11 |pages=82–95 |url=http://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/roosmalen-200802.html |archive-url=https://arquivo.pt/wayback/20091014093223/http%3A//www.smithsonianmag.com/science%2Dnature/roosmalen%2D200802.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2009-10-14 |accessdate=2008-07-20 }}</ref> He is also an activist in the protection of the Brazilian rainforest.<ref>http://marcvanroosmalen.info/bijlage/curriculum_vitae.pdf{{Dead link | date=August 2025 | fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> Van Roosmalen was awarded the [[Dutch honours system|honour]] of officer in the [[Order of the Golden Ark]] by [[Prince Bernhard of Lippe-Biesterfeld|Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands]] in 1997.<ref>http://marcvanroosmalen.org/pages/aboutpag.html{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.onderscheidingen.nl/nl/medailles/konhuis/ga.html |title=Orde van de Gouden Ark<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=July 1, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930224239/http://www.onderscheidingen.nl/nl/medailles/konhuis/ga.html |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
Van Roosmalen studied biology at the [[University of Amsterdam]] and did four years of doctoral fieldwork beginning in 1976 studying the [[red-faced spider monkey]] in [[Suriname]].  He later did two more years of work in [[French Guiana]], following which he published the book ''Fruits of the Guianan Flora''.  In 1986 he was hired by the [[INPA]] (Brazilian National Institute of Amazonian Research, where he initially thrived.  During this period, he launched a [[non-governmental organization]] focused on creating wilderness preserves in the deep Amazon.  He became a naturalized Brazilian citizen in 1997.  Marc considers [[Alfred Russel Wallace]] his icon and is an advocate of Wallace's [[River barrier hypothesis|"river barrier" hypothesis]] that the major rivers of the Amazon basin serve as barriers that create separate genetically distinct evolutionary regions.<ref | name="TrialofaP" />

==Personal life==
Marc grew up in [[Tilburg]], a city in the southern part of the [[Netherlands]].  His father was a chemist.  He met and married his first wife while living in [[Utrecht]], where he had moved for school at age 17. They had two sons. In early 2008, he divorced his first wife and married his Brazilian girlfriend.<ref | name="wired" />

==Controversies==
In 2002, he was fined by the [[IBAMA]] (Brazilian Ministry of the Environment's Enforcement Agency) for illegal transportation of monkeys and [[orchids]] from the unexplored Amazonian region of Serra do Aracá. In April 2003, Van Roosmalen was fired from his senior scientist job with the federal institute INPA for alleged 'illegal' export abroad of environmental genetic samples.<ref name="folha">[http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ciencia/ult306u307606.shtml Pesquisador holandês é condenado no Amazonas.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018134740/http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/ciencia/ult306u307606.shtml |date=October 18, 2007 }} - Folha Online</ref>

In 2007, he was arrested by the Brazilian government for illegally keeping orphaned monkeys in a monkey refuge at his house in Manaus and for misappropriation of Brazilian public funds.<ref name="folha" /> He was sentenced to 14+ years in prison.  Van Roosmalen claims that he over and over applied for permits for his monkey preserve. He was placed in the notorious Raimundo Vidal Pessoa Penitentiary in Manaus-AM.  At one point Van Roosmalen shared a cell with two violent crack addicts whose drug debts he had to pay to stay alive.<ref name="wired">{{cite magazine |last=Ratliff |first=Evan |title=Why Does This Prominent Amazon Researcher Face 14 Years in Prison for Biopiracy? |date=19 May 2008 |magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/2008/05/mf-monkeybusiness/}}</ref> After three months in 'hell on earth', he was set free on appeal.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/28/science/28biop.html?8dpc | work=The New York Times | title=As Brazil Defends Its Bounty, Rules Ensnare Scientists | first=Larry | last=Rohter | date=28 August 2007 | accessdate=12 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2007/06/hero_biologist_jailed_in_brazi.php |title=DutchNews.nl - 'Hero' biologist jailed in Brazil<!-- Bot generated title --> |date=June 21, 2007 |access-date=June 22, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626042721/http://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2007/06/hero_biologist_jailed_in_brazi.php |archive-date=June 26, 2007 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Van Roosmalen told a ''[[Wired (website)|Wired]]'' news reporter that he has a video of two ex-policemen knocking on his door immediately after tucking revolvers into their pants.  Believing that he would be killed if he stayed, he and his partner Vivian Garcia went on the run to the Caribbean Island of Margarita with no plans to return to their home in [[Manaus]] as of August 2007.<ref name="wired" /> In exile, on contract with a Dutch publishing house, Van Roosmalen began to write popular-scientific books about his life in the Amazon. In December 2008, he was fully absolved from all alleged "crimes against Mother Nature" by the Supreme Court in Brasilia-DF.

In 2010, Marc van Roosmalen received a grant from the Scholar Rescue Fund of the [[Institute of International Education]] in NY. He was appointed as a Distinguished Scholar in Residence for the 2010-2011 academic year at Bard College.<ref>{{cite web |title=World-Renowned Biologist and Amazon Researcher Marc van Roosmalen Joins Bard College as Visiting Scholar and Gives Public Talk on October 26 |url=https://www.bard.edu/news/releases/pr/fstory.php?id=1974 |website=Bard College |accessdate=28 September 2020}}</ref>

[[Van Roosmalen's dwarf porcupine]] and [[Van Roosmalen's dwarf marmoset]] are discovered by and named after him. He named the [[Prince Bernhard's titi]] after the late [[Bernhard of Lippe-Biesterfeld|Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands]], co-founder and former president of the WWF.
